content: Potassium thiocyanate is a chemical compound with the molecular formula KSCN. It is a significant salt of the thiocyanate anion, which is classified as one of the pseudohalides. This compound is notable for its relatively low melting point compared to most other inorganic salts. Use in Chemical Synthesis Aqueous potassium thiocyanate (KSCN) reacts almost quantitatively with lead nitrate (Pb(NO₃)₂) to produce lead thiocyanate (Pb(SCN)₂). This lead compound has been utilized in the conversion of acyl chlorides into thiocyanates. Additionally, KSCN facilitates the transformation of ethylene carbonate into ethylene sulfide. For this reaction, KSCN is first melted under vacuum conditions to eliminate water. In a related chemical process, KSCN converts cyclohexene oxide into the corresponding episulfide. Furthermore, potassium thiocyanate serves as the starting material for the synthesis of carbonyl sulfide. Other Uses Dilute aqueous solutions of potassium thiocyanate are occasionally employed in film and theater to create moderately realistic blood effects. The solution can be applied to a surface or maintained as a colorless liquid. When it comes into contact with a ferric chloride solution, the reaction produces a blood-red solution, mimicking the appearance of blood.
